name: Canary
summary: A two-line poster headline, 'CANARY TESTS IT.' on a yellow highlight bar, then a long proof sequence of agent transcripts, diffs and replayed failures.

observations.hero: Left-aligned on near-black: a 'Backed by Y Combinator' chip, a grey line '[agent] WRITES YOUR CODE.' whose agent name rolls between Claude, Codex, Cursor and Copilot, then 'CANARY' in yellow and 'TESTS IT.' in black on a yellow bar. Below are one paragraph, a single yellow 'COPY THE PROMPT' button and the mono caption 'One line for your agent.' The bottom edge shows the top of a mock agent window with a floating 'Start Demo' pill.
observations.typography: The measured h1 element is 32px, weight 400, −0.01em tracking, in Archivo Black. The largest display text measures 124px Archivo Black, set in caps. Body text is 17px Archivo with 1.7 line height and a 64ch measure. Nav, eyebrows, buttons and terminal text are in a monospace face; IBM Plex Mono is among the three measured families. Section heads repeat the heavy all-caps display style.
observations.visual_system: The ground is a warm near-black with sparse yellow constellation dots and lines. A single yellow accent carries CTAs, the highlight bar and active tabs. Red and green mark failures, diffs and two of the stats. Surfaces are thin-bordered dark panels, terminal panes, code diffs and a case-file timeline. There are no photographs; the diagrams are a dot sphere of failure paths and an integration fan-in.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → agent demo window (thread + diff) → stats row (10K+ bugs, 12K+ hours, 80%+ fix rate, 55% P0/P1) → 01 Install (3 steps, copyable prompt) → 02 Problem (three points + failure-path sphere) → 03 How it works (4 tabs) → 04 Where it runs (4 tabs) → 05 Integrations diagram → 06 Examples (4 case tabs + case file) → 07 Research (QA-Bench bar chart) → 08 closing CTA → footer.
observations.interaction: I clicked '02 ONE CLICK, TWO RECORDS' in Examples, then on a second load '02 Run' in How it works. Neither tab stayed selected: the How-it-works row advanced on its own from 01 to 03 while I waited. On load the hero agent name rolled between names, stats counted up from 0 when scrolled into view, and the 'Start Demo' pill stayed fixed over the demo. With reducedMotion set to reduce, the running-animation count was 0–1 versus 5 by default. Hero frames taken 2s apart were identical in both modes.
observations.accessibility: Several small mono captions and labels sit at low contrast on near-black: 'One line for your agent.', stat labels and footer column heads. The floating 'Start Demo' pill overlaps the demo window's title text. On mobile, footer links measured 18px tall and the demo message input 22px; the demo's 'Claude Code' tab is clipped at the right edge. No horizontal overflow was measured. Tab rows that advance on their own change content while it is being read.
observations.mobile: The nav collapses to the logo and a hamburger. The display drops to 44px, and the headline wraps to four short lines with the bar still behind 'TESTS IT.' The demo window becomes one tall column, thread above diff. The stats stack vertically, install steps stack, 4-tab rows become 2×2 grids and Examples tabs stack vertically. The integrations fan-in becomes a 2-column chip grid with arrows down to Canary, then Codex. The page grows to 11,532px.

principles: Make the claim evidence itself: replay a real failure as terminal output plus a case file (test, break, root cause, fix) instead of listing features.
When the buyer's tool is the entry point, make the primary CTA something that runs inside that tool (a copyable prompt) rather than a signup form.
Keep one accent colour, use it for action and emphasis only, and reserve red/green for pass/fail meaning.
Number sections like a document (01 / INSTALL … 08 / YOUR MOVE) so a long proof sequence stays navigable.
interpretation.fit: Developer tools where trust comes from seeing a concrete failure caught, such as testing, security or observability. It would be wrong for a non-technical buyer who cannot read diffs or terminal logs.
interpretation.risks: At ten sections and over 9,000px, the page asks for a lot of scrolling before the closing CTA. Self-advancing tabs ignored my clicks, so visitors can lose control of what they read. The heavy all-caps display face is loud on every section head, which flattens the hierarchy. The stats are unsourced on the page.

limitations: On the first exploratory load the page rendered before its styles applied (cream ground, stacked nav, monospace headings). Later loads rendered the dark design, so I treat the first as a load-timing artefact, not a variant.
Could not confirm whether tab clicks are ignored by design or lost to timing; two attempts on different tab rows did not hold.
The 'Start Demo' walkthrough was not started.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

interpretation.fit: Suits consumer or prosumer desktop utilities with a playful voice and a founder-led audience. It would be wrong for a compliance or banking product, where faked OS chrome and meme objects would undercut trust.

limitations: The full-page 1440 capture was missing from the input bundle; desktop sequence comes from live viewport captures.

Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Atomarine
summary: A full-bleed render of floating platforms with a full-width uppercase claim along the bottom edge makes an unbuilt industrial system feel concrete.

The uppercase h1 'NUCLEAR DATA CENTERS AT SEA' runs the full content width along the bottom edge, with a yellow-dot label above it and a yellow 'SCROLL TO SEE THE PLATFORM ↓' cue at right. Body measured 14px/1.3. Section heads are mixed-case and medium weight; small uppercase labels with a dot mark each section (THE CONSTRAINT, SCALE, POWER).

Imagery is photoreal pictures of platforms, ships and a desert data center; abstract dot-field and particle graphics accompany stats; the scale section uses white line drawings of platform layouts. A large outlined wordmark closes the footer.

Section content appeared only after it entered view; captures taken under 0.5s after a scroll step showed blank sections. In the scale section, line drawings and a statement slid horizontally as I scrolled. Under reduced motion the hero video element still reported playback (about 1.5s elapsed).

At 390, the footer email and back-to-top links are 16px tall, and a DOM check found 16 links or buttons with no text, aria-label or title. Contact form fields have visible labels. Measurement record marks the reduced-motion rule as unverified. No horizontal overflow.

principles: When the product is physical and not yet built, lead with a render that shows its scale in context and state the category in the headline.
Order the narrative as constraint, answer, scale path, then transition story so a sceptical buyer meets the problem before the claim.
Use a before/after slider when the pitch is a substitution, so the visitor performs the change themselves.
Restrict accent colour to one hue for actions and labels so it survives across dark, white and photographic sections.
interpretation.fit: Suits deep-tech, energy and infrastructure companies selling to investors, operators and partners, where one bold image carries the thesis. It would be wrong for a self-serve software product that needs to show an interface and a sign-up path.
interpretation.risks: Reveal-on-scroll content leaves sections blank to fast scrollers, screenshots and possibly assistive tools. The page shows renders and claims (4X faster, <1.1 PUE) without sourcing on the homepage. A single Contact action and 14px body text limit depth for technical buyers, and the hero video kept playing under reduced motion.

limitations: Embedded YouTube video was not played.
Stat claims and renders are company statements; whether imagery is rendered or photographed was not verified.
Whether reveal sections fail on real mobile devices or only in headless scrolling was not determined.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

principles: Put a running, believable product moment directly under the headline so an infrastructure API reads as a working thing, not a diagram.
Offer a copy-to-agent or install path beside the primary button when the buyer will hand setup to a coding agent.
Use language tabs that swap install command and sample together so each developer sees one complete path.
Repeat the hero's exact action pair at the end of the page so a convinced reader does not have to scroll back.
interpretation.fit: Suits developer APIs and infrastructure whose output is an event (a call, a message, a webhook) that can be dramatised in a loop. It would be wrong for a product whose value is slow or invisible, such as data residency or audit logging, where a looping fake demo would mislead.
interpretation.risks: The hero demo is scripted and keeps moving under reduced motion. Dense dark-on-green cards and small grey captions cost legibility. The mascot, gradients and bento make the page long (8,663px desktop) before pricing, and code samples clip on phones.

limitations: The hero call demo was not verified as connected to a live service; it appeared scripted.

Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

principles: For a sensitive consumer category, lead with a human photograph and a plain-language claim before any interface.

interpretation.fit: Suits consumer health, wellness and care apps where reassurance and empathy matter more than feature density. It would be wrong for a clinician-facing or enterprise tool, where buyers need workflow, integration and compliance detail up front.
interpretation.risks: The long photographic page depends on lazy-loaded images and reveals that rendered blank, grey or as alt text in captures. Stock-feeling portraits risk reading as generic. The desktop page is very long (14,619px), and the product UI itself is barely shown.

limitations: Live visits on 2026-10-19 returned HTTP 502 twice; no control was operated and reduced motion was not tested live.
The desktop full-page capture stops at 9,000px of 14,619px; later desktop sections were inferred only from the 390 capture.

Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

Cards are rounded, off-white with soft borders; one pricing tier is inverted to near-black. Client logos sit in individual tiles. Colour beyond cream, brown and black comes only from client logos.
observations.page_sequence: Photo hero with split CTA panel → '500+ startups, scaleups, and enterprises trust General Legal' testimonial masonry + logo tiles → interior photo with 'Expert judgment for every matter' and four numbered steps (Start Today, Priced Up Front, Accessible Expertise, Legal at AI Speed) → 'A new kind of firm...' attorney portrait cards → 'The best lawyers, now on every matter' practice-area card → 'Simple, transparent pricing' four tiers → FAQ → closing CTA and footer.
observations.interaction: Operated FAQ item '4. How does pricing work?': it expanded with a tinted row, the plus became a minus, and an answer with a 'pricing page' link appeared. On scroll, the large 'Expert judgment' line sat over the interior photo while step cards passed; the practice-area labels were at different angles in live and stored captures. The fixed header moved out of view when scrolling down. Nothing visibly moved on the first screen in either normal or reduced-motion loads.
observations.accessibility: Cream text and the outlined 'Start a matter' button sit on a photograph; the right half of the description runs over the lighter document area. Where 'Expert judgment for every matter' crosses the photo, letters darken against the wood, reducing legibility. At 390 the menu icon is two thin lines. The hero image stops about 15px short of the right edge at both widths. No horizontal overflow measured.
observations.mobile: The photo is cropped tighter on the document; headline, description and two full-width stacked buttons fill the lower half, and the panel's explanatory labels are dropped. Testimonials reduce to one card per row, logos to a two-column grid, attorney cards to a horizontal row cut at the edge. The 'Expert judgment' photo-and-steps section does not appear (measured sections 6 vs 7). Pricing tiers stack.

principles: Split the hero CTA into two labelled paths ('talk to us' vs 'start now with a fixed quote') when buyers arrive at different levels of readiness.
Use a still-life of the actual work product (a contract) as hero imagery to signal the service without stock-photo people.
Put real prices on the homepage when the business model's differentiator is pricing; it turns a positioning claim into something checkable.
Show the named experts with credentials early when trust in a new kind of firm depends on who does the work.
interpretation.fit: Suits professional services re-packaged as products (legal, accounting, advisory) where trust, people and pricing transparency matter more than a software UI. Wrong for a self-serve software tool, where atmosphere photography would delay showing what the product does.
interpretation.risks: The photographic mood costs legibility in two places (hero copy over the image, display text over the interior photo). The page is long (12,104px at 1440) and the mobile version silently drops the four-step process section, so phone visitors lose the explanation of how engagement works.

limitations: Measurement record reports a video element, but nothing played on the first screen in this browser; headless Chromium may not support the video format, so hero motion was not verified.
Rotation of the practice-area labels was inferred from two captures; its trigger was not observed.
YC page location field is blank, so no geography evidence is recorded.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Known
archetype_note: Manifesto splash: one centered text poem on black plus an app CTA; a brand poster, not an editorial page.
summary: The homepage is a single centered manifesto on black, a short protest against swiping, ending in one Apply to Join button.
round: Pear portfolio, Pre-seed → Seed (year not shown)

viewports.desktop: 1440 × 900: rendered, scrolled; no in-page control at this width (menu toggle operated at 390)

observations.hero: knowndating.com redirects to known.com. The first screen is pure black with a wordmark top-left, three text links and an outlined Apply to Join pill top-right, and a narrow centered block of short sentences in four stanzas ('Profiles told us nothing...', 'Not a game. Not a job. Not a gamble.'). There is no headline, image or product shot above the fold.
observations.typography: Measured h1 is 16px, weight 500, 0em tracking, family -apple-system, and holds 'Known: your pocket matchmaker, a swipeless dating app'; it is not the visible copy. Largest measured display text is 18px. The manifesto is set as small, centered, regular-weight sans lines with blank-line stanza breaks; body measured 16px / 1.5. The wordmark is a custom lowercase logotype; only -apple-system is in the measured families.
observations.visual_system: Black ground (#000-like) with off-white text; footer shifts to a slightly warm near-black. The bottom CTA is a light grey pill with a metallic sheen. Press logos (Union-Tribune, LA Times, WSJ and more) are dimmed grey. A QR code sits in the desktop footer. A full-viewport video element exists but was paused and not visible in any capture.
observations.page_sequence: Manifesto stanzas → 'This is Known.' → Apply to Join button → 'Available on iOS & Android, featured in' press logos → footer (QR code, Discover / Here / Elsewhere link columns, wordmark, copyright). Measured as one section, 1317px tall at 1440.
observations.interaction: At 390 I operated the hamburger: it became an X and a black panel dropped down with three large links (How it Works, Guidelines, Journal) over the top of the manifesto. With motion on, manifesto lines changed between captures and the 390 full capture shows lines fading in from a blur. In motion mode only three press logos showed, the first cropped at the edge; under reduced motion all lines rendered at once, eight press logos appeared in a static grid, and paired captures were identical.
observations.accessibility: Small grey 'Available on iOS & Android' text and dimmed press logos sit on black at low apparent contrast. The visible manifesto is not the h1; the h1 is a 16px line. Transparent sticky nav lets manifesto text scroll beneath the links. No horizontal overflow measured. Mobile header CTA and hamburger are comfortably sized.
observations.mobile: Nav links collapse into a hamburger and the Apply to Join pill moves beside it. Stanzas rewrap to the same centered column. The footer QR code is replaced by an app icon labeled 'Tap to Install', and link columns go two-up then stack. Page grows to 1601px.

principles: When the product's pitch is a rejection of category norms, a short manifesto can carry the whole first screen without any product imagery.
Pair a single-action page with one CTA repeated in the nav and at the end of the text, so the reader never has to search for the next step.
Swap a desktop QR code for a direct install link on mobile so the download path fits the device.
interpretation.fit: Consumer apps with a clear stance and an application or waitlist gate, where tone matters more than features. Wrong for any B2B or technical product whose buyer needs to see how it works.
interpretation.risks: The page explains almost nothing: no screenshot, no how-it-works, no pricing, and the real h1 is hidden from sight. The line-by-line blur reveal delays reading on load, and the low-contrast grey details may fail contrast checks.

limitations: Could not operate an in-page control at 1440; the only interactive elements were nav links and Apply to Join, which leads to an application flow.
A video element was present but paused; whether it plays under other conditions was not verified.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Prized
summary: A saturated cobalt brand world, with ASCII art, a split-flap board and a giant clock, shows always-on dev boxes as scenes rather than feature lists.

observations.hero: A white YC announcement strip sits above a full-bleed cobalt hero. Left: a three-line light-weight headline, one-line subhead, white 'Create my box' and outlined 'Read the docs' pills, a '$30 of credit. No card.' note, and a black terminal chip with a curl install command and copy button. Right: a large cloud drawn in ASCII characters over a dotted field.
observations.typography: Measured h1 77.4px, weight 300, -0.035em tracking, line-height 1.0, family prizedSans; body 17px / 1.6 prizedSans with an 87ch measure. JetBrains Mono is used for commands, labels and the split-flap board; a 'mockFace' family appears in product mocks. The display reads as a light grotesque with tight tracking.
observations.visual_system: Three grounds alternate: cobalt blue, black, and white rounded cards. Imagery is all typographic: ASCII clouds and laptops, a split-flap departures board, a 24-hour bar chart, a huge 17:58 clock. Pills for CTAs, mono for anything machine-like. Footer ends with an oversized ghosted wordmark and asterisk logo. A floating 'Watch the launch 1:02' video tile sits bottom-right.
observations.page_sequence: YC strip → blue hero → 'New: Sandboxes' strip → black 'Check on it from anywhere' dashboard mock → white '24 hours a day' bar chart → black 'Ports are localhost' split-flap board plus terminal → white card 'Files go both ways' with ASCII laptops → pinned blue 'At six you close the lid' clock scene → 'A clear advantage' table vs Codespaces and Coder → blue 'Your box is two minutes away' CTA → black footer.
observations.interaction: I clicked 'on Windows?' under the install chip: the command changed to 'irm https://prized.dev/install.ps1 | iex' and the caption to 'Windows PowerShell · on macOS or Linux?'. The dashboard mock's filter tabs could not be clicked; an overlay intercepted pointer events. With motion on, the hero ASCII cloud and the split-flap characters changed between captures, and the clock scene stayed pinned across about 1,800px of scroll. Under reduced motion, paired captures at top and mid-page were identical.
observations.accessibility: White text on cobalt reads clearly at display sizes, but small light-blue mono captions ('macOS and Linux') on blue look low-contrast. The copy button is icon-only but exposed an accessible name. Product-mock buttons are present in the DOM but blocked from pointer input. No horizontal overflow measured. Mobile CTA pills are large.
observations.mobile: h1 drops to 34px over four lines; the YC strip shortens to 'Backed by Combinator'; 'Sandboxes' leaves the nav. The ASCII cloud moves below the install chip, which wraps the curl command with a backslash continuation. Sections stack single-column; the comparison table stays tabular. Measured content width 249px; page 9473px with 9 sections.

principles: Turn each product claim into one memorable scene (a clock, a port board, a sync diagram) instead of a feature grid.
Put the real install command in the hero with a copy button and an OS toggle, so a developer can act without leaving the first screen.
Build imagery from the product's own medium, here text characters, so the brand and the subject reinforce each other.
Gate ambient motion on prefers-reduced-motion so the scenes still read when frozen.
interpretation.fit: Developer infrastructure and CLI-first tools whose buyers trust terminal output more than illustrations. Wrong for a regulated enterprise purchase where buyers need security, compliance and integration detail early.
interpretation.risks: Scene-per-section pacing makes a long page (8,845px) with little dense information; the pinned clock scene costs a lot of scroll for one idea. Mock UI that looks clickable but is not may frustrate. Small mono captions on blue risk contrast failures.

limitations: Did not play the launch film or inspect the docs; the hero ASCII cloud's motion was observed only as changes between two captures.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: End Close
summary: A framed split hero pairs a plain reconciliation promise with a live-looking matching table and an 'Agent resolved' toast, then walks the workflow tab by tab.

observations.hero: Redirects to www.endclose.com. A white page with a wordmark, a centered outlined nav pill (Product, Company, Docs) and a violet 'Learn more on a call' button. The hero is a hairline-framed two-column box: left a four-line headline, subhead, violet 'Book a demo' and 'Find out more →'; right a reconciliation table mock (24 / 14 matched / 10 unmatched) with an 'Agent resolved · EXC-004' toast. A four-cell stat row closes the frame. A cookie banner overlays the lower left.
observations.typography: Measured h1 60px, weight 600, 0em tracking, line-height 1.0, family ui-sans-serif (system stack); body 18px / 1.6 with a 45ch measure. Geist Mono is used for amounts, references and the feature-chip cloud. Hierarchy is weight and size only; no display face.
observations.visual_system: White and very light grey bands, hairline borders with small crosshair marks at frame corners, one violet accent for primary buttons, active tab rules and highlighted chips. Imagery is product UI only: tables, a data-source picker modal, a reconciliation overview with record counts. Green/red amounts and status pills come from the mocks. One testimonial card uses a blue gradient panel with a headshot.
observations.page_sequence: Framed hero + stat row → 'From origination to closed books' three tabs (Ingest, Automated matching, AI agents) over a product mock → Sunbound testimonial → 'Everything you need out of the box' four tabs + mono feature-chip cloud → 'Compare us to building in-house or buying a legacy vendor' three-column table → 'Trust your numbers. Stop chasing them.' CTA card → footer with SOC badge.
observations.interaction: I clicked the 'Automated matching' tab: its top rule turned violet and the mock changed from an 'Add a data source' modal to a 'TabaPay vs CRB' reconciliation overview (102,009 of 161,396 reconciled). On scroll the nav re-formed as a centered floating pill holding the logomark, links and CTA. The active tab's rule filled like a progress bar; that fill kept running under reduced motion, while the hero stayed static in both modes.
observations.accessibility: Inactive tab titles and descriptions are light grey on white, a contrast concern. Mono chips are small. The cookie banner covers part of the first screen at both widths. At 390 the word 'reconciliation' extends past the hero frame's right border, though no page-level horizontal overflow was measured. A progress animation continues under reduced motion.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to a hamburger (measured nav height 0). h1 drops to 48px; the table mock moves below the CTAs and the stat row stacks two-up. Tabs stack vertically, the comparison table becomes stacked per-row blocks, and the page more than doubles to 9387px. The cookie banner covers roughly the lower quarter of the first screen.

principles: Show the exception being resolved, not just the dashboard: a single toast like 'Agent resolved · Duplicate refund' carries the AI claim more credibly than a slogan.
Tie each workflow tab to its own product state so clicking a step changes what the buyer sees.
Use a three-way comparison (you, build in-house, legacy vendor) when the real competitor is the buyer's own engineering team.
Reserve a monospace face for money and identifiers so financial data reads as data.
interpretation.fit: B2B finance, payments ops and other back-office software where buyers want proof of correctness and audit trails. Wrong for a consumer product or anything that needs emotional brand pull over evidence.
interpretation.risks: The layout follows a common B2B SaaS pattern and is visually hard to tell apart from peers. The hero headline breaks its frame on mobile, the cookie banner hides first-screen content, and the tab progress fill ignores reduced motion. The 99.999% claim sits without visible sourcing.

limitations: Whether the workflow tabs auto-advance on their own was not confirmed.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Andera
summary: A centered, lavender-tinted hero hands off to a scroll-pinned walkthrough in which mock audit workpapers fill in and log checks as you scroll.

observations.hero: A lavender announcement bar ('We raised $37M led by Lightspeed...'), then a white nav with six links and an outlined Book a demo. The centered headline 'Audit just got / a whole lot easier' has 'lot easier' in a purple gradient and small selection-handle squares and dots around it. Below: a two-line subhead, a dark 'Book a demo' button, a 'Trusted by audit teams at' logo row, and the top of a 'My Tasks' dashboard mock.
observations.typography: Measured h1 64px, weight 550, -0.01em tracking, line-height 1.1, family Manrope; body 16px / 1.5 Manrope with a 52ch measure. Inter is also present. Section headings repeat a two-tone pattern: dark indigo plus a purple-gradient phrase ('end-to-end.', 'your controls', 'security.').
observations.visual_system: Near-white ground with lavender tints, dark-indigo text and a purple accent. Faint fine-line wave patterns at the hero edges; small rounded pill labels ('Features', 'Explore GRC', 'Security') above each section. Imagery is product UI: task dashboards, a spreadsheet with an audit log, RCM and testing tables, plus concentric rings around a SOC badge and a team photo.
observations.page_sequence: Announcement bar → centered hero + logos → dashboard mock with progress chart → 'Fieldwork automated, end-to-end' pinned three-step (Control Testing, Evidence Gathering, Exception Management) → 'A home for your controls' tabs (RCM, Risks, Dashboard) → 'Focus on risk, not reconciliation' three staggered numbered cards → 'Enterprise-grade security' → 'Give your team their best hours back' CTA → 'We are the industry experts' about + photo → FAQ accordion → footer.
observations.interaction: I clicked the 'Dashboard' tab under 'A home for your controls': the caption changed to 'Track anything and everything...' and the two-table RCM/Testing mock was replaced by an 'Acme Inc' dashboard (58% completed, workload bar, control rows). While scrolling, the features section pinned and its step titles lit in turn. Under reduced motion the hero was static, but audit-log check icons still appeared between captures in the features mock.
observations.accessibility: Several texts are pale lavender-grey on near-white ('Trusted by audit teams at', inactive step titles, card body text), a contrast concern. Measured mobile body text is 12px. The 1440 full-page capture shows a long blank band where the pinned section sits. No horizontal overflow measured. The FAQ uses buttons for questions.
observations.mobile: The announcement bar wraps to two link lines; nav reduces to Book a demo plus a hamburger. h1 drops to 44px and still fits on two lines. Logos wrap to three rows. Tabs, the three numbered cards and the about section stack single-column; the dashboard mock is scaled down rather than recomposed. Measured body text drops to 12px; page 9587px.

principles: Let a pinned scroll section narrate a multi-step workflow, with one step lit at a time and its mock filling in beside it.
Show the work being done (timestamped audit-log lines, 'Control passes with no deviations') rather than a static result when selling automation to auditors.
Repeat one heading device, like a gradient tail phrase, across sections to give a light-ground B2B page a recognizable rhythm.
Answer the buyer's incumbent question (RPA, existing GRC tool) directly in the FAQ.
interpretation.fit: Enterprise compliance, audit and GRC tools sold to professional users who need to see their own artifacts (RCMs, workpapers, exceptions). Wrong for a self-serve product, where a long pinned walkthrough delays the moment of trying it.
interpretation.risks: Pale lavender text costs legibility, and 12px mobile body text is small. The pinned section adds scroll length and renders as empty space in static captures and possibly for crawlers. Some log animation continues under reduced motion. The decorative selection handles around the headline say little about the product.

limitations: The FAQ accordion and the other two pinned feature steps' mocks were not inspected in detail.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.
